title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, 1986). M is a set of 'objects' (tame closed pieces). They are ordered by inclusion ≤, have intersections X∩Y, a boundary ∂X ≤ X and a restriction X'_L. A symmetric, antireflexive relation ∥ ('disjoint/étrangers') generates supports by biorthogonality. For X in M, X° ⊂ M is the set of 'interior' objects X' ≤ X with X' ∥ ∂X; Lemma 1 (L1) says X° ≠ ∅. The theorem under proof (pages 94-96) concerns families F of mutually compatible objects. The map F ↦ S_F = Supp(∪_{X∈F} X°) should be injective and compatible with Inf, Sup and complements; parts a), b), c).

Page 94 reduces a) (S_A ⊂ S_B ⇒ A ⊂ B) to Lemma 8: if B∪{X} is admissible and Supp(X°) ⊂ S_B, then X ∈ B. This page proves the contrapositive. If X ∉ B, we need Z ∈ M with Z ∥ ∪_{Y∈B} Y° but not Z ∥ X°. Take any Z ∈ X° (possible by L1). Then not Z ∥ X°, by antireflexivity of ∥ (Z is non-empty). Z ∥ Y° for every Y ∈ B follows from the next lemma.

Lemma (numbered 9, or 4 in the machine reading). Let X, Y ∈ M be compatible with X ≠ Y. Then X° ∥ Y° (a fortiori X° ∩ Y° = ∅).

Proof. Take X' ∈ X° and Y' ∈ Y°, and put L = X∩Y. By an axiom ('Ab D'), X' ∥ Y' reduces to X'_L ∥ Y'_L. Compatibility means L = X, or L = Y, or L ≤ ∂X and L ≤ ∂Y.
- In the third case, X'_L ≤ X'_{∂X} = ∅ and Y'_L ≤ Y'_{∂Y} = ∅, so both traces are empty and the pieces are disjoint.
- Otherwise, say L = Y, i.e. Y ≤ X with Y ≠ X. Then Y ≤ ∂X, so Y' ≤ Y ≤ ∂X. Since X' ∥ ∂X, we get X' ∥ Y'.

Geometrically: the open cells of distinct cells in a compatible family (a 'cell complex') are pairwise disjoint, and each open cell is non-empty. These are exactly hypotheses a), b) of the abstract lemma on p.96.

The page then begins b). Knowing compatibility with Sup, compatibility with Inf reduces to compatibility with complements, which is c). Page 96 abstracts everything into a lemma on an orthogonality space (M, ∥): pairwise orthogonal non-empty sets A_i give a complete Boolean embedding of P(I) into the ortholattice Σ of supports (biorthogonally closed sets).
errors: The second inequality is written Y'_L ≤ Y'_{∂X}; it should be Y'_{∂Y} (slip).

The step Y ≤ X, Y ≠ X ⇒ Y ≤ ∂X is used without justification. It must come from the definition of compatibility, or from a property of the objects (proper subobjects in the family lie in the boundary). Otherwise it is a gap.

The hypothesis is read 'X ≱ Y' in the machine transcription. That is inconsistent with the proof, which treats the case Y ≤ X. The hypothesis must be 'X, Y compatible' (as in Lemma 8's admissibility condition).

The next page carries the marginal note 'Faux ?' on the abstract generalization. The full Boolean-embedding claim, including complements S_{A∖B} = S_A ∩ ∁S_B, is indeed doubtful in a general orthogonality space without orthomodularity-type hypotheses. This page's specific claims are fine.

ideas.what: Open cells of distinct compatible cells are mutually disjoint (X° ∥ Y°). The proof reduces disjointness to traces on the intersection L = X∩Y.
ideas.modern_name: Disjointness of open cells in a regular CW / polyhedral or stratified complex
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 only sketches tame topology; no such axiomatics published

ideas.what: Recovering a sub-family B of a complex from the support of the union of its open cells (Lemma 8). The separating object is chosen inside the interior X°.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of subcomplex ↦ underlying closed set; separation via biorthogonal closure

ideas.what: Defining 'supports' purely from an abstract symmetric antireflexive disjointness relation ∥ on objects, via biorthogonal closure. This yields a complete ortholattice in which a tame topology is developed.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / polarity closure (Galois connection), ortholattice of closed sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck bases an axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame topology) on an abstract disjointness relation ∥ and the ortholattice of biorthogonally closed 'supports'. This is the framework of orthogonality spaces from quantum logic (Dacey, Foulis–Randall). Tame/o-minimal or stratified topology was not developed this way in the literature.
missed.quote: Alors X° ∥ Y° (a fortiori, X° ∩ Y° = ∅)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a point-free, relation-based foundation for tame topology. Supports would form an ortholattice in which cell complexes give Boolean subalgebras. This could interface with locale/point-free topology. The idea is modest and incomplete (cf. 'Faux ?' on the next page).

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine lemma: open cells of distinct compatible cells are disjoint, used for injectivity. The only mildly notable feature is the orthogonality-space style axiomatization of tame topology in the 1986 unpublished Analysis situs notes, and that belongs more to the surrounding pages.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'dans tout ce qui suit je montrerai ceci' should read 'donc tout revient à montrer ceci :'.
'et d'expliquer le' is probably 'et d'appliquer le' (or 'd'utiliser le').
Lemma number likely 'Lemme 9' (following Lemme 8 on p.94), not 'Lemme 4'.
Hypothesis 'X ≱ Y' is likely a compatibility symbol (X, Y mutually compatible), not a negated order relation.
'Y'_L ≤ Y'_{∂X}' as written; mathematically it should be Y'_{∂Y}.
'Inf (la seule [?] pour la sup)' should read 'Inf (le sachant pour le sup)'.
